evidence.model: adult mouse digit amputation: regenerative distal P3 versus non-regenerative more proximal injury contexts
evidence.mechanical_observation: Regenerative and non-regenerative digit environments differ in ECM organization and measured tissue mechanics; AFM/force mapping is reported in the source program.
evidence.loss_of_function: HA depletion after regenerative digit-tip amputation impairs regenerative outcomes and promotes a more fibrotic/non-regenerative repair program.
evidence.gain_of_function_or_rescue_like: HAPLN1-overexpressing fibroblast transplantation in a normally non-regenerative digit context changes ECM state/mechanics and improves bone-repair/regrowth-associated outcomes relative to controls.
evidence.public_replay_subgate: GSE274858 and associated public analysis code permit replay of perturbation-associated single-cell transcriptional analyses.

why_not_pure_mechanics: The causal manipulations alter hyaluronic-acid biology/ECM composition and organization together with mechanical state. Measured mechanics plus a coupled ECM intervention do not isolate mechanics from matrix chemistry.
why_not_strict_timing_root: The existing strict MECHANICAL_STATE_TIMING_GATE requires delayed direct physical retuning after an established repair/scar state. The TOPA screen found later DPA measurements and post-amputation interventions but did not establish the required delayed post-establishment direct physical-retuning design. OUTCOME_TIME_IS_NOT_INTERVENTION_TIME.
